clue.text: Course picked up by detective

parts.note: to pick something up is to notice or spot it
dick is old slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: A golf or race course has been noticed by a sleuth on the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a golf course or a route; it is a course of a meal. SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert is one course of a meal, and this currant suet pudding is a classic British example.

clue.text: Devised series of games

definitions.meaning: something devised has been fixed or arranged
in tennis a group of games forms one unit of a match

explanation.definitionFit: A setter fixes a task, and in tennis a run of games makes up one unit of a match.

clue.text: Star group performing outside port

indicators.note: the word for performing is placed around the port, sitting outside it

parts.note: a performer who is on stage is performing
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A band of celebrities plays a gig beyond the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' tempts you toward a celebrity, but with 'group' it means a constellation; 'outside' wraps the performing word around the port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a well-known constellation, a group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Date extract

definitions.meaning: to date someone is to escort them out for an evening
to extract a tooth or a stain is to remove it

explanation.definitionFit: Escorting someone on a date and removing something are both senses of the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Deal, perhaps, going nowhere in particular

definitions.text: Deal, perhaps, going nowhere in particular

parts.words: Deal, perhaps, going nowhere in particular
parts.note: deal is a kind of pine timber; timber floating aimlessly on the sea is going nowhere in particular

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a bargain or a hand of cards, but it is softwood timber, and floating wood is aimless.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber carried by currents and washed up has no destination, drifting wherever the sea takes it.

clue.text: Metal (not lead) obtained in this form?

indicators.note: the metal loses its leading letter, so its opening is dropped

parts.note: tin is a metallic element
got means obtained

explanation.surface: A metal other than lead might be produced in this shape, the clue asks.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not lead)' looks like a remark about which metal it is, but it beheads TIN to IN. The definition is the closing 'this form', with the whole clue painting the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelted metal is commonly cast into a block of standard shape for storage and trade.

clue.text: Very funny first line replaced by quiet poet

indicators.note: the opening letter that stands for line gives way to the abbreviation for quiet

parts.note: something killing is extremely funny
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A hilarious opening verse is swapped out by a softly spoken versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first line replaced by quiet' swaps the first L (line) in KILLING for P. The poet is Rudyard Kipling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote verse such as If and Gunga Din, so he is a poet.

clue.text: Reported excessive speed

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the word for excessive is heard rather than written

parts.note: high prices are excessive ones

explanation.surface: A news story about driving much too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH and HIE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an archaic verb meaning to hasten or go quickly.

clue.text: Tricky situation, breaking a top tooth'- might it have been chipped?

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A front tooth breaks, and the dentist wonders whether it was chipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges A TOP TOOTH. The closing question jokes that a potato might be turned into chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversial issue that nobody wants to handle is likened to something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Goldsmith's teacher was certainly not so frivolous

definitions.text: Goldsmith's teacher was certainly not so frivolous

parts.words: Goldsmith's teacher was certainly not so frivolous
parts.note: Oliver Goldsmith's village schoolmaster in The Deserted Village amazed rustics because one small head could carry all he knew, so his head was full

explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith is the poet Oliver Goldsmith, not a metalworker: his schoolmaster's head was famously crammed with knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A frivolous, silly person is said to have nothing in their skull, the opposite of the learned schoolmaster.

clue.text: Catch fish moving in a small stream

parts.note: a catch is a trick or snag
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler hooks a fish travelling up a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' and 'fish' look like angling verbs; they are a snag and a named fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that flows in a thin stream runs slowly, drop by drop.

clue.text: Propose to offer accommodation

definitions.meaning: to propose a candidate is to nominate them
to give a guest a bed for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Nominating a candidate and housing a guest overnight are both senses of the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: After study, order companion

indicators.note: after places the word for order following the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
to sort is to put in order

explanation.surface: Having studied, someone arranges a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the word for order behind the word for study; con in the sense of learning by heart is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or partner, especially of a monarch.

clue.text: Little consolation for Flora on this farm

definitions.meaning: a phrase for comfort that hardly helps
Flora Poste is the heroine of Stella Gibbons's comic novel set on a Sussex farm

explanation.walkthrough: Flora is not plant life but Flora Poste, heroine of Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor solace is proverbially chilly, and the same phrase names Gibbons's farm.

clue.text: I record going in to hear a series of Greek tragedies

indicators.note: going in to means these pieces enter the word for hear

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A diarist writes up a trip to see some ancient drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in to' sets the pieces inside; 'hear' is the courtroom sense, where a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus's Oresteia is a set of three linked plays, the classic three-part work.

clue.text: Was dependent, having thin time

parts.note: lean means thin

explanation.surface: Someone relied on others during a hard, meagre period.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to put your weight on them, a past-tense verb of support.

clue.text: Died away from place in Yorkshire -in American cemetery

indicators.note: away from means the abbreviation for died is taken out of the place

parts.note: Darlington is a town in north-east England, historically on the edge of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone passed away far from their Yorkshire home, buried in a US graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes D (died) from DARLINGTON, a town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The national military burial ground in Virginia, across the river from Washington, bears this name.

clue.text: Where to put plaster, having to use excessive stock?

definitions.text: Where to put plaster, having to use excessive stock?

parts.words: Where to put plaster, having to use excessive stock?
parts.note: a sticking plaster goes on top of a skin scrape; stock here is livestock eating too much pasture

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words for first aid: a plaster goes on top of a scrape. 'Stock' is farm animals, not supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting too many animals feed on pasture strips and damages it.

clue.text: Nobleness shown by architect's plan

definitions.meaning: loftiness or grandeur of character or style
a drawing showing one face of a building

explanation.definitionFit: Loftiness of mind and an architect's drawing of a building's face are both senses of this noun.

clue.text: Poet is to drop round when president receives king

indicators.note: receives means the president's name takes the royal abbreviation inside
is to drop means a letter must be taken out of the president's name

parts.note: Calvin Coolidge was the 30th US president
O is round in shape
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A versifier is to call in when the head of state welcomes a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to drop round' looks like paying a visit, but signals losing a ring-shaped letter from the president; 'receives' takes in Edward Rex. The poet is Samuel Taylor Coleridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner and Kubla Khan.

clue.text: Singer formally dressed?

definitions.meaning: Paul ... was an American bass singer and actor
read as two words, someone with ceremonial gowns on

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer describes someone with ceremonial gowns on.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was a famous American bass, known for Ol' Man River.

clue.text: Worry over issue

definitions.meaning: to dwell anxiously on something
offspring, a family of young

explanation.definitionFit: Dwelling moodily on a matter and a family of young are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Arrange to marry one March it's nonsense to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene means the word for nonsense comes between the letters of the name

parts.note: Beth is one of the March sisters in Little Women
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a wedding, saying a spring date is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' is not the month but the family in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women; 'to intervene' sets the nonsense word inside the sister's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise someone in marriage is to engage them formally.

clue.text: Take away place I book in small coach

indicators.note: place, followed by in, tells us to set these letters within the word for take away

parts.note: minus means take away, as in subtraction

explanation.surface: Instructions for booking a seat on a little bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place ... in' puts I + B inside MINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibus is a small passenger vehicle, a little coach for a group.

clue.text: Farm animal sticking hard in ooze

indicators.note: in, with sticking, means the hard letter is pushed inside the word for ooze

parts.note: to seep is to ooze
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A ewe gets stuck fast in the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking ... in' puts H inside SEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A wool-bearing ruminant kept in flocks on farms.

clue.text: Poorly, can't help out — indigestion remedy needed

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are in poor shape and must be rearranged

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Feeling ill and unable to get help, someone needs something for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' rearranges CANT and AID.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion comes from too much stomach acid, and a tablet that neutralises it is the remedy.

clue.text: Get up, taking care at first with leg

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of care is used

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Advice on rising carefully, starting with one leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes C from 'care'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend or mount is to go upwards, as one does on a ladder.

clue.text: Gallant gentleman, one implicated in conspiracy

definitions.meaning: Captain Lawrence ... of Scott's polar expedition, memorialised as a very gallant gentleman
Titus ... fabricated the Popish Plot of 1678

explanation.definitionFit: Captain Oates walked out to die in Antarctica, and Titus Oates invented a Catholic plot against Charles II.

clue.text: Expression of opinion to the left of our correspondents

definitions.text: Expression of opinion to the left of our correspondents

parts.words: Expression of opinion to the left of our correspondents
parts.note: in a newspaper the leader column often sits beside the letters from readers; to the left also hints at political leaning

explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' hints at a political leaning, but it means placed beside: the leader column sits next to the readers' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article states the paper's own view on an issue.

clue.text: Form of illumination provided guidance

definitions.meaning: a light-emitting diode, a kind of lamp
showed the way, the past tense of lead

explanation.definitionFit: A light-emitting diode is a type of lamp, and showing the way is the past of 'lead'.

clue.text: Cure for effect of mild 'sunburn

definitions.meaning: to cure leather is to treat a hide
skin darkened by sun

explanation.definitionFit: Treating a hide to make leather and skin browned by the sun share one word.

clue.text: Horribly behind with tricky input, but finish off early

indicators.note: horribly means the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lagging behind with a difficult data entry wants to finish early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horribly' and 'tricky' both rearrange BEHIND and INPUT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something at its very beginning, like pinching off a flower before it opens.
